findings.checklist_item: - [ ] 79d5 AC4 is updated to add the third permitted outcome: 'or documented with a primary-source citation (e.g. `jira.text.field.character.limit` property in jpm.xml + JRASERVER-28519) recorded both at the binding and on this ticket', so the verifier can accept the provenance-citation approach the ticket comment directs.
evidence: 79d5 AC4: 'the real DC comment ceiling is either MEASURED (with the measurement recorded here) or explicitly marked UNVERIFIED at the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding, so a reader cannot mistake an assumption for a decision'
79d5 ticket comment: 'THE COMMENT CEILING IS NOW ESTABLISHED FROM PRIMARY SOURCES. AC4 can be satisfied by DOCUMENTING PROVENANCE rather than by measurement or by marking the binding UNVERIFIED'
79d5 ticket comment: 'AC4 is met by recording THIS provenance (the property name + JRASERVER-28519) at the binding, replacing an assumption with a citation'
The ticket comment introduces a third allowed outcome that is absent from the AC text
findings.finding: AC4 scope-narrowing in child 79d5: the AC as written permits exactly two resolutions — MEASURED (with the measurement recorded on the ticket) or UNVERIFIED (label applied at the binding) — but the ticket comment establishes a third resolution path that the AC text does not permit: documenting the 32767 ceiling via primary-source provenance (jpm.xml `jira.text.field.character.limit` + JRASERVER-28519 citation added at the binding). A completion verifier applying AC4 literally ('either MEASURED... or explicitly marked UNVERIFIED') will reject the planned provenance-citation approach because it is neither a measurement nor an UNVERIFIED annotation. This is the bypass-annotation AC-contradiction pattern: the child plans to satisfy the criterion via a path the criterion text doesn't name.
scenarios: An implementer adds a code comment citing jpm.xml and JRASERVER-28519 at the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding — exactly what the ticket comment directs — but the completion verifier reads AC4 and sees neither a measured value recorded on the ticket nor the string UNVERIFIED in the code, and marks the AC unmet.

A different implementer, reading AC4 without the ticket comment, marks the binding UNVERIFIED (the second allowed outcome) — which is now incorrect because the value IS verified by primary sources — creating a misleading comment in production code.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend 79d5 AC4 to read: '... or documented at the binding with a primary-source citation (property name + canonical JRASERVER/JRACLOUD reference) recorded on this ticket — so a reader cannot mistake an assumption for a decision.' This makes the planned resolution formally acceptable without changing the intent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-sentence positive rationale in the epic plan (or the operator-attested AC bullet) explaining why manual apply-and-revert attestation is chosen over mutation-testing tooling: the two-record requirement (ticket comment + committed module-level comment block) is what makes the evidence durable and diff-reviewable after session end, which tool-generated reports stored outside the tree do not satisfy.
evidence: Plan states: 'A pin nobody has seen fail is not evidence. Copied terminal output showing the mutated code and the resulting FAIL, pasted as a child-ticket comment, satisfies this criterion; it is attested rather than CI-checkable because a mutation is applied and reverted in a working tree and therefore leaves no repo artifact to inspect'

The constraint (no repo artifact) is stated, but the positive rationale for manual attestation over tooling is absent — the plan says WHY CI-gating won't work, but not WHY manual attestation is preferred over running mutmut/cosmic-ray which CAN produce recorded output without a committed artifact
Child ticket cedc also records the mutation format requirement without explaining why this mechanism was chosen over tooling
findings.finding: The epic plan's mutation-attestation mechanism (operator-attested terminal output recorded as ticket comments + committed module-level comment blocks) lacks a stated positive rationale at the epic level — only the structural constraint that makes CI-gating infeasible is cited. Without a positive rationale, an implementer who prefers a mutation-testing tool (mutmut, cosmic-ray) has no guidance on why manual attestation was chosen, and could inadvertently substitute an approach that generates durable CI artifacts but covers a different mutation surface.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — operator-attested bullet; 'PRIORITY FRAMING' section
scenarios: An implementer substitutes cosmic-ray or mutmut, generates a mutation report artifact, and satisfies the 'seen it fail' requirement — but the report is a generated file outside the diff and cannot be treated as a committed comment block. The AC says 'committed, diff-reviewable repo artifact' for the module-level comment, which tooling does not produce in the right form.
An implementer reads the AC as only requiring a ticket comment, skips the module-level comment block entirely, and the evidence disappears from the repo when the session ends.
findings.suggested_fix: In the operator-attested AC bullet, add: 'Manual apply-and-revert is chosen over a mutation-testing tool because the two-record requirement — a ticket comment AND a committed module-level comment block — is what makes the evidence durable and diff-reviewable after the session ends; a tool-generated report stored outside the tree satisfies neither record.'

findings.finding: The `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` call-site inventory in child ticket `bd9e` (incorporated into the epic's AC3) was explicitly derived by `git grep` alone, without also running `find_referencing_symbols`. The plan text states: 'A repo-wide `git grep -n _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` (string grep, not just a semantic reference search — the LSP does not see string/attribute access reliably) returns exactly seven sites.' This is a positive statement that only one of the two required derivation methods (string grep) was run. A complete re-derivation requires both: `find_referencing_symbols` for structural references AND string grep for attribute-access, `getattr`, and dynamic uses. The plan chose grep as the sole stated method even though structural references (e.g., an import alias that binds the name under a new identifier in a third module) would only be caught by the symbol graph.
